title: SLO-aware dual-region handoff with approximate KV synchronization
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: Implement an active-active dual-region handoff mechanism for the hosted API edge that is aware of per-route SLOs and preserves streaming session continuity where possible. Scope: gateway routing, KV cache sync/approximate snapshotting, progressive traffic shifts, per-session token stitching, SLO-driven circuit governor, and load-shedding policies. Out of scope: full stateful user session replication and cross-region KV strong consistency.
updates: 2026-01-22 — Maya Chen: Created ticket. Drafted goals and high-level design. Initial risk list includes KV divergence and streaming token expiry.

2026-02-03 — Rafael Ortega: Spike completed: implemented prototype approximate KV snapshot using prefix checksums and per-epoch deltas. Observed 95% key convergence in 1s for typical request patterns in lab.
2026-02-18 — SRE review by Anika Patel: requested explicit SLO integration points and runbook hooks. Recommended canary plan with traffic floor and guardrail metrics.

2026-02-28 — Eng design review: decided to use progressive traffic steps (5%, 25%, 60%, 100%) with epoch anchoring and short-lived sticky tokens for in-flight streams. Circuit governor thresholds enumerated.
2026-03-05 — Rafael Ortega: Added load-shedding prototype at gateway level for route-weighted shedding and token-preserving abort handler for streaming continuations.
2026-03-10 — Maya Chen: QA experiments scheduled on perf cluster; telemetry queries for token-preservation ratio and KV divergence instrumented. Preparing PR for canary gating logic.
design_decisions: Use 'approximate' KV synchronization: snapshot + compacted deltas to minimize cross-region bandwidth while achieving acceptable cache alignment for most streaming sessions.
Progressive traffic shift steps to limit blast radius and provide telemetry windows to detect SLO regressions.
Introduce a circuit governor that integrates route-level SLO burn rates and regional capacity signals to trigger partial or full load-shedding.
Token-stitching model for streaming: issue a short-lived handoff token representing KV epoch + stream offset; target resumption by compatible replica within TTL.
Fallback model variants for degraded regions to maintain latency SLOs when full KV alignment can't be achieved.
acceptance_criteria: Canary shift executed automatically across epochs with roll forward/rollback based on SLO alarms.
Streaming sessions resumed on target region at >= 90% success rate for sessions under 60s at lab load.
End-to-end P99 tail latency for critical routes remains within configured SLOs during a progressive handoff in 90% of canaries.
Circuit governor triggers and load-shedding policies reduce downstream error rates while keeping graceful degradation paths operational.
Operational runbook documented with step-by-step rollback, cutover, and postmortem templates.
risks_and_mitigations: KV divergence causing failed resumption — mitigate via conservative delta window, epoch anchors, and transient prefix fallbacks.
Token expiry during long-running streams — mitigate by extending TTL during handoff and issuing resumable offsets.
Unintended canary spillover — mitigate with strict routing quotas and kill-switch in console tied to telemetry.
Cost of cross-region sync — mitigate by sampling keys and only syncing hot prefixes; tune by telemetry.
Complexity of circuit governor tuning — mitigate by staged experiments and default conservative thresholds.
tests_and_experiments: Lab: scale test with synthetic streams (1k concurrent streams) to validate token stitching success rate across KV divergence levels.
Chaos: region failover simulation during heavy write bursts to measure SLO burn and circuit governor behavior.
Perf: latency histogram comparison pre/post-handoff for p50/p95/p99 on critical routes.
Canary: automated progressive shift with stepwise SLO gates and automatic rollback on burn rate anomaly.
owner_oncall_notes: If pTokenPreserve < 85% during step transition, engage rollback: pause canary and route back to primary region.
If SLO burn rate > 5x baseline for 5 minutes, trigger circuit governor full shed for the affected route.
implementation_tasks: Build gateway handoff controller and routing plugin (RFC + initial PR).
KV sync service: implement snapshot + compact delta producer and consumer.
Extend session token format to include epoch and offset; implement stitch/resume in runtime.
Implement circuit governor and gateway-level load shed policies with per-route knobs.
End-to-end tests, chaos scripts, and canary automation pipeline.
qa_notes: Pre-canary checklist: smoke tests, traffic fencing, telemetry retention for 48h, and rollback playbook verified.
Edge cases to validate: multi-party streams, partial-kv-miss path, and retries with idempotency keys.
estimated_rollout: Week 1: internal spike and unit tests.
Week 2: integration test in perf cluster and design reviews.
Week 3: canary with limited routes and progressive steps.
Week 4: expand canary coverage and monitor for regressions before broader rollout.
